subject: Maths
title: Rounding decimals to decimal places
subtitle: Decimals — All Operations · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can round decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places.

key_vocab.definition: Rounding to decimal places (d.p.) means shortening a decimal to a given number of digits after the decimal point.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can round decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Rounding -- Rounding to decimal places (d.p.) means shortening a decimal to a given number of digits after the decimal point.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Look at the digit AFTER the one you want. 5 or above: round up. Below 5: round down.
3.147 to 2 d.p. → look at 7 (third d.p.) ≥ 5 → 3.15
Critical digit decides

Key examples:
  ✓ 3.147 to 1 d.p. = 3.1  (4 < 5, round down)
  ✓ 3.147 to 2 d.p. = 3.15  (7 ≥ 5, round up)
  ✓ 6.998 to 2 d.p. = 7.00  (rounds up to 7.00)
  ✗ 3.147 to 1 d.p. = 3.2  (look at 4, not 7)
  ✗ 6.998 to 2 d.p. = 6.10  (should be 7.00)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – rounding to 1 d.p.
  Round 4.63 to 1 decimal place.
  We want 1 d.p.: keep one digit after the point
  Look at the 2nd d.p.: 3
  3 < 5, so round down: 4.6
  = 4.6
  (The digit after is 3 (less than 5), so we keep 4.6.)

Example 2 – rounding to 2 d.p.
  Round 7.386 to 2 decimal places.
  We want 2 d.p.: keep two digits after the point
  Look at the 3rd d.p.: 6
  6 ≥ 5, so round up: 7.39
  = 7.39
  (The 6 forces the previous digit (8) to round up to 9.)

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Round the answer appropriately.

(a) 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333... to 2 d.p.
(b) π = 3.14159... to 3 d.p.
(c) £7 shared among 3 people (to nearest penny)
(d) 22 ÷ 7 = 3.14285... to 2 d.p.

sections.title: Mixed rounding
sections.content:
Round to the number of d.p. stated.

(a) 6.4812 to 1 d.p.
(b) 3.0962 to 2 d.p.
(c) 0.999 to 1 d.p.
(d) 12.3456 to 3 d.p.
(e) 7.005 to 2 d.p.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 3.147 to 1 d.p. = 3.1
✗ Look at the digit you want to keep, not the next one
✓ 6.998 rounded to 2 d.p. = 7.00
✗ 5 always rounds down
✓ Rounding 4.95 to 1 d.p. gives 5.0
